cancer_indication: HER2-positive breast cancer (metastatic disease after prior trastuzumab/taxane therapy, or adjuvant therapy for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant treatment).
moa: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) combines the anti-HER2 antibody trastuzumab with the microtubule inhibitor DM1 via a stable linker. It binds HER2 (ERBB2) on cancer cells, blocks HER2-driven signaling and can elicit ADCC, then the HER2–T-DM1 complex is internalized via receptor-mediated endocytosis. In lysosomes, DM1 is released and binds β-tubulin to inhibit microtubule function, inducing mitotic arrest and triggering apoptosis.

REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVERE.description: Constitutive downstream signaling driven by overexpressed ERBB2 (HER2) receptor activity.
REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVERE.interpretation: HER2 overexpression is the key biomarker for T-DM1 activity in breast cancer, and HER2-driven signaling underpins tumor proliferation and survival in HER2-positive disease.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High HER2 overexpression/signaling indicates abundant target for T-DM1 binding and internalization, enabling efficient intracellular delivery of DM1 and trastuzumab-like signaling blockade.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: HER2 pathway “up” can still be functionally bypassed by downstream/parallel survival signaling (e.g., PI3K–AKT activation) or HER2 heterogeneity/selection, reducing dependence on HER2 and blunting benefit.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2+ tumors show weaker “signaling” signatures yet retain high surface HER2 protein for ADC binding/internalization, allowing DM1 payload killing despite muted pathway readouts.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low/heterogeneous HER2 biology (low effective target density) reduces ADC binding and internalization, yielding primary resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (signature-level): Adaptive HER2 upregulation can occur under pressure, but if HER2 remains targetable and internalization/lysosomal processing is intact, higher target can still coincide with response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (signature-level): Non-responders can show compensatory reactivation/upregulation of HER2 signaling (or selection of HER2-high clones) while resistance is maintained via downstream bypass or defective intracellular processing.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: T-DM1 engagement reduces effective HER2 signaling (trastuzumab component) while delivering DM1 that disrupts microtubules → cytotoxicity and clinical benefit in HER2+ breast cancer.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Apparent HER2 pathway downshift can still be resistant if payload delivery is blocked (impaired endocytosis/lysosomal proteolysis/lysosomal export) or if strong bypass signaling prevents apoptosis.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2_IN_CANCER.description: Cancer-associated ERBB2 (HER2) receptor signaling and its downstream proliferative and survival pathways.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2_IN_CANCER.interpretation: ERBB2 signaling is central to HER2-positive breast cancer biology and is directly engaged by the trastuzumab component of T-DM1.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: ERBB2-in-cancer pathway up reflects HER2-driven biology with sufficient receptor density for T-DM1 binding/internalization and DM1-mediated mitotic catastrophe.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ERBB2 pathway up does not guarantee response if HER2 is heterogeneous or intracellular trafficking/lysosomal processing is defective, limiting active catabolite exposure.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Tumors with lower pathway transcription but preserved HER2 protein expression can still respond because ADC efficacy depends heavily on antigen-mediated uptake rather than pathway “activity” signatures.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Down ERBB2-in-cancer signaling commonly tracks with low/patchy HER2 target availability, lowering ADC binding/internalization and causing resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (signature-level): Therapy can increase apparent ERBB2 signatures via feedback or immune/stromal admixture; if ADC processing remains intact, response can still occur.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Rebound ERBB2 signaling or selection for ERBB2-high clones plus downstream bypass can sustain growth despite T-DM1 exposure.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective target engagement and internalization decrease functional ERBB2 signaling and deliver DM1, improving outcomes in HER2+ disease (e.g., EMILIA/KATHERINE).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ERBB2 signaling down with resistance can reflect target loss/heterogeneity or intracellular resistance nodes (low lysosomal proteolysis, SLC46A3 loss), preventing DM1 from reaching tubulin.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: PI3K–AKT–mTOR survival and growth signaling downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases, including HER2.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: This pathway is described as a key downstream HER2 axis in HER2-positive breast cancer and is mechanistically relevant to the anti-proliferative effects associated with HER2 targeting.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Highly PI3K-AKT-driven tumors may still respond if they remain HER2-high and proliferative, making them vulnerable to DM1’s anti-mitotic payload despite survival signaling.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K–AKT–mTOR hyperactivation can reduce dependence on HER2 and raise apoptosis threshold, contributing to reduced ADC efficacy in some settings.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lower PI3K survival tone makes cells less able to tolerate mitotic stress from DM1, favoring apoptosis/mitotic catastrophe after T-DM1 uptake.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with low PI3K signaling, resistance can occur via non-PI3K mechanisms (poor internalization, lysosomal dysfunction, drug efflux), limiting DM1 exposure.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (adaptive): Transient PI3K activation from stress/feedback can appear early after treatment, yet adequate intracellular DM1 delivery can still trigger mitotic catastrophe and response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent PI3K–AKT–mTOR activation (e.g., PTEN loss/PIK3CA-driven survival) can enable escape from DM1-induced death and is a common bypass theme in HER2 therapy resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: T-DM1’s trastuzumab component can dampen PI3K signaling downstream of HER2 while DM1 kills dividing cells, reinforcing sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even when PI3K readouts fall, resistance can persist if lysosomal processing/export is impaired (no cytosolic catabolite) or if ABC efflux prevents effective intracellular DM1.

HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.description: RAS–MAPK signaling programs associated with KRAS/RAS pathway activation and proliferative signaling.
HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.interpretation: RAS/MAPK signaling is described as a downstream pathway linked to HER2 signaling, relevant to proliferation and potential pathway bypass in HER2-driven tumors.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: KRAS/MAPK-up tumors can still be sensitive if they remain highly proliferative and HER2-targetable, making them susceptible to anti-microtubule payload effects.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MAPK-driven signaling can act as a HER2-bypass growth axis, reducing reliance on HER2 inhibition and contributing to diminished response.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low baseline MAPK bypass signaling increases dependence on HER2 biology and makes cells less able to compensate for trastuzumab-like signaling blockade plus DM1 cytotoxicity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Resistance with low MAPK signatures can occur via trafficking/lysosomal defects or drug efflux, independent of KRAS/MAPK activity.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (stress response): A transient KRAS/MAPK “up” signature can reflect treatment stress while cells still undergo mitotic catastrophe from sufficient DM1 exposure.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive MAPK reactivation is a classic bypass route after HER2 engagement and can support survival/proliferation despite ADC exposure.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective HER2 engagement can reduce downstream MAPK signaling while payload-induced mitotic arrest drives tumor cell death.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: MAPK down with resistance can occur if the main resistance node is intracellular (lysosomal catabolism/export loss) rather than signaling bypass.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Regulation of mitotic entry and the G2/M checkpoint machinery that controls progression through mitosis.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: The DM1 payload induces mitotic arrest; pathway activity reflecting mitotic cycling is mechanistically relevant to DM1-mediated cytotoxicity in tumor cells.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High G2/M checkpoint/mitotic activity indicates rapid cycling, increasing vulnerability to DM1-mediated microtubule disruption and mitotic arrest.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some highly cycling tumors evade death via mitotic slippage/checkpoint adaptation or defective apoptosis, yielding reduced response despite a strong G2/M program.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even with lower baseline cycling, substantial HER2-mediated ADC uptake can still deliver enough DM1 to trigger lethal mitotic errors in the dividing fraction.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Slow-cycling/low-mitotic tumors have fewer cells traversing mitosis, reducing susceptibility to anti-microtubule payloads.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: DM1 catabolites bind tubulin and disrupt spindle formation, increasing mitotic checkpoint signaling (G2/M arrest) and driving mitotic catastrophe.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Mitotic arrest can be prolonged without effective apoptosis (e.g., survival pathway dominance), allowing eventual escape and resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Strong responders can show a drop in bulk G2/M signatures due to rapid tumor cell elimination and reduced proliferative fraction.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce mitotic arrest can reflect insufficient intracellular DM1 exposure (poor internalization/lysosomal release or drug efflux), leading to resistance.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: E2F-driven transcriptional programs associated with cell-cycle progression and S-phase entry.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F activity is described as reflecting cell-cycle progression, which is mechanistically relevant because T-DM1 requires dividing cells for DM1-mediated mitotic effects.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High E2F target expression indicates active proliferation and S-phase entry, correlating with susceptibility to downstream mitotic disruption by DM1 in cycling cells.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Proliferative tumors can still resist if ADC trafficking is defective (low lysosomal catabolism/export) or if MDR transport limits intracellular payload accumulation.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some low-proliferation tumors respond if HER2-mediated uptake is very efficient and the dividing compartment is selectively eradicated by DM1.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Quiescent/slow-cycling biology reduces dependence on mitotic processes targeted by DM1, favoring resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (timing): Early on-treatment samples may still show high E2F as cells attempt cycling before lethal mitotic failure occurs, yet overall response can follow.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent E2F/proliferation after therapy implies inadequate DM1 action (efflux/processing defects) or strong bypass survival, consistent with resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective DM1 action and trastuzumab-like signaling blockade reduce proliferative programs (including E2F targets) as cells arrest and die.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: E2F down can coincide with resistance if tumor shifts to a slow-cycling drug-tolerant state while maintaining viability (minimal mitotic engagement).

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Intrinsic apoptosis and execution programs mediated by caspases and BCL2-family regulated mitochondrial pathways.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptotic machinery is described as enabling tumor cell death after DM1-induced damage and HER2 pathway effects.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline pro-apoptotic priming lowers the threshold for DM1-induced mitotic catastrophe to trigger executioner caspases and cell death.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Despite apoptosis signaling, resistance can occur if intracellular DM1 delivery is insufficient (endocytosis/lysosome/export defects) or if anti-apoptotic dominance persists.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some apoptosis-low tumors still respond when payload exposure is high enough to cause catastrophic spindle failure beyond salvage.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low apoptotic competence (high survival/anti-apoptotic programs) supports persistence after mitotic stress, contributing to resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lysosomal release of DM1 catabolites disrupts microtubules → mitotic arrest/mitotic catastrophe and activation of apoptosis pathways.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis may be initiated but incomplete (e.g., strong PI3K survival or anti-apoptotic rewiring), yielding partial response and eventual resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (bulk effect): Bulk apoptosis signatures can fall after effective tumor debulking because fewer tumor cells remain to contribute transcript signal.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to activate apoptosis after exposure indicates ineffective payload delivery (processing/export/efflux issues) or intrinsic apoptosis resistance.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Interferon-γ–associated immune activation and inflammatory transcriptional responses.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: Immune activation is described as relevant to Fc-mediated immune effector functions (e.g., ADCC) associated with the trastuzumab component of T-DM1.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: A pre-existing IFN-γ/TIL-inflamed microenvironment can enhance trastuzumab-mediated immune effector functions (ADCC) and may synergize with ADC-mediated tumor killing in HER2+ breast cancer.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: IFN-γ-high tumors may still resist if immune suppression dominates (e.g., checkpoint upregulation/exhaustion) and intracellular ADC resistance (lysosomal/efflux) limits tumor killing.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Even with low IFN-γ signaling, T-DM1 can be effective through direct HER2-targeted DM1 delivery and microtubule disruption (immune-independent cytotoxicity).
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Profound immune-desert tumors can lose the added benefit of antibody-mediated effector functions and, if coupled with intracellular resistance nodes, exhibit poorer response.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: ADC-induced tumor cell stress/death can promote immune activation; immunogenic cell death features have been linked to improved T-DM1 response in HER2+ breast cancer models.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: IFN-γ increase can coexist with resistance if adaptive immune checkpoints or suppressive myeloid/Treg programs counteract immunity and tumor-intrinsic ADC resistance persists.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Successful tumor clearance can reduce IFN-γ signatures over time as antigen burden falls and immune infiltrates contract.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistent immune suppression/exclusion (no IFN-γ response) can mark non-response, especially when combined with limited tumor cell kill from intracellular ADC resistance.

GOBP_RECEPTOR_MEDIATED_ENDOCYTOSIS.description: Internalization of receptor–ligand complexes through receptor-mediated endocytosis and vesicular trafficking.
GOBP_RECEPTOR_MEDIATED_ENDOCYTOSIS.interpretation: T-DM1 requires HER2 binding followed by internalization for intracellular delivery of DM1, making endocytic uptake mechanistically central.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High receptor-mediated endocytosis capacity supports HER2-bound T-DM1 internalization, a prerequisite for lysosomal catabolism and DM1 release.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Internalization can still be non-productive if HER2–ADC complexes preferentially recycle rather than traffic to lysosomes, limiting payload release.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even with lower global endocytosis signatures, strong HER2 density and alternative uptake routes can permit enough ADC internalization for response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Poor internalization is a direct resistance mechanism for ADCs—insufficient intracellular delivery prevents formation of active DM1 catabolites.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Productive T-DM1 therapy requires and effectively engages endocytic uptake of HER2–ADC complexes, increasing intracellular trafficking toward lysosomes.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Endocytosis may increase yet still be resistant if downstream steps fail (lysosomal proteolysis, lysosomal export of lysine-MCC-DM1, or high efflux).

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Reduced endocytosis signatures after response can reflect fewer viable HER2+ tumor cells remaining rather than impaired uptake.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Acquired resistance frequently involves decreased ADC internalization/altered trafficking, limiting lysosomal delivery and payload liberation.

GOBP_LYSOSOMAL_TRANSPORT.description: Trafficking to lysosomes and transport processes that support lysosomal degradation and downstream handling of catabolites.
GOBP_LYSOSOMAL_TRANSPORT.interpretation: Lysosomal processing is described as necessary for DM1 release after internalization, linking lysosomal transport/function to payload availability.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Efficient lysosomal trafficking/function supports proteolytic degradation of the antibody and liberation of lysine-MCC-DM1, enabling tubulin targeting.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with high lysosomal transport, resistance can occur if lysosomal proteolysis is impaired or if catabolite export to cytosol is blocked (e.g., SLC46A3 loss).

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Partial lysosomal impairment may still allow response if sufficient catabolism/export occurs in a subset of cells with high HER2 uptake.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Reduced lysosomal proteolytic activity/trafficking limits generation and cytosolic availability of active DM1 catabolites, a documented T-DM1 resistance mechanism.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: On-target action involves endosome→lysosome delivery and lysosomal processing; intact lysosomal transport correlates with effective payload activation.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Lysosomal trafficking may be intact, yet resistance persists if lysosomal membrane export of lysine-MCC-DM1 is defective (SLC46A3-related) or if ABC transport removes payload from cytosol.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Lysosomal signatures can decline after response due to reduced tumor cellularity and altered composition of the sampled tissue.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Acquired downregulation of lysosomal processing/export reduces active catabolite availability and is a central resistance axis for non-cleavable linker DM1 ADCs.

KEGG_ABC_TRANSPORTERS.description: ATP-binding cassette transporter-mediated efflux of xenobiotics and drugs (e.g., MDR1/P-gp).
KEGG_ABC_TRANSPORTERS.interpretation: Drug efflux is described as mechanistically relevant to intracellular DM1 exposure after payload release, impacting retention of the cytotoxic component.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Despite ABC transporter expression, strong HER2-mediated uptake plus high intralysosomal catabolite production can sometimes overcome partial efflux and still yield response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Maytansinoids (DM1) are substrates for efflux pumps such as MDR1/P-gp; high ABC transporter activity lowers intracellular payload exposure → resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low efflux capacity increases intracellular retention of DM1 catabolites after lysosomal processing, favoring effective tubulin inhibition and cell death.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with low ABC transporter signatures, resistance can still arise from upstream failures (poor internalization/lysosomal catabolism/export) that prevent payload action.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some responders may show induced transporter expression as a stress response, yet payload exposure remains sufficient to cause mitotic catastrophe.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Therapy can select for clones with increased MDR1/ABC transporter activity, reducing effective intracellular DM1 and driving acquired resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Reduced efflux after treatment is consistent with sustained intracellular payload exposure and effective tubulin inhibition/cell death.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Efflux down may still be resistant if the limiting step is payload activation (lysosomal proteolysis/export) rather than cytosolic drug retention.

GOBP_CAVEOLIN_MEDIATED_ENDOCYTOSIS.description: Endocytic uptake mediated by caveolin-dependent vesicles and caveolae-associated internalization routes.
GOBP_CAVEOLIN_MEDIATED_ENDOCYTOSIS.interpretation: Caveolin-associated uptake is described as influencing T-DM1 internalization, linking this endocytosis route to intracellular delivery of DM1.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Caveolin-1/caveolae-mediated endocytosis can enhance T-DM1 internalization and has been linked to greater chemosensitivity to T-DM1 in HER2+ breast cancer models.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Caveolar uptake may be non-productive if trafficking favors recycling or if lysosomal processing/export is defective downstream of internalization.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low caveolin signatures can still allow response via alternative endocytic routes or high HER2 abundance enabling sufficient uptake.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Reduced caveolae/lipid-raft uptake can lower T-DM1 internalization, limiting lysosomal delivery and payload release.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: On-treatment enhancement of caveolae-mediated uptake increases intracellular delivery of HER2-bound T-DM1, improving payload activation and response.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Uptake can increase yet resistance persists if lysosomal proteolysis/export (e.g., SLC46A3) is limiting or if ABC efflux dominates.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Caveolin signatures can drop after response due to reduced tumor content and altered tissue composition rather than causal resistance.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Loss/downregulation of caveolin-dependent internalization reduces productive T-DM1 uptake and is consistent with acquired resistance.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High cyclin B1 expression is described as indicating active cycling into mitosis, where the DM1 payload is most effective at inducing mitotic arrest.
Higher CDC20 is described alongside cyclin B1 as supporting mitotic entry/progression, aligning with T-DM1’s requirement for dividing cells to enable DM1-mediated mitotic blockade.
Elevated caveolin-1 is described as enhancing T-DM1 uptake via caveolin-mediated endocytosis, increasing internalization and payload delivery.
Upregulation of SH3GL1 (endophilin A2) is described as promoting efficient HER2–T-DM1 internalization; reduced levels suppress cytotoxicity in the report.
Higher SLC46A3 is described as facilitating lysosomal export of DM1 into the cytosol, supporting payload release and cytotoxicity.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Overexpression of MDR1/P-gp (ABCB1) is described as effluxing the DM1 payload, reducing intracellular drug concentration and promoting lack of response.
High PLK1 activity is described in resistant models as promoting mitotic progression and dampening T-DM1 cytotoxicity; PLK1 inhibition can resensitize in the report.
Constitutive PI3K–AKT activation is described as a known resistance mechanism in HER2-positive breast cancer that can blunt HER2 inhibition effects relevant to T-DM1.
KRAS/RAS hyperactivation is described as bypassing HER2 blockade by sustaining RAS/MAPK signaling, which can undermine the anti-proliferative signaling impact of HER2 targeting.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Reduction or loss of HER2 expression is described as decreasing the available target for T-DM1 binding, impairing delivery of the DM1 payload and contributing to lack of response.
Downregulation of cyclin B1 is described as preventing cells from entering mitosis where DM1 acts, reducing cytotoxic effect in the report.
Downregulation of CDC20 is described as preventing mitotic progression needed for DM1-mediated arrest and downstream apoptosis.
Reduced caveolin-1 is described as impairing T-DM1 internalization and lowering cytotoxicity through diminished endocytic uptake.
Reduced SH3GL1 is described as impairing HER2–T-DM1 internalization and suppressing cytotoxicity by limiting delivery to lysosomes.
Loss of SLC46A3 is described as preventing lysosomal export of DM1, trapping the payload and reducing tumor cell killing.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive subtypes: Trastuzumab emtansine efficacy is strictly tied to HER2 status; it is effective in all HER2-positive subtypes (including HER2-enriched or Luminal B/HER2+ cancers) and is indifferent to hormone receptor or BRCA/HRD status per se.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR-positive/HER2-negative (Luminal A/B): HR-positive/HER2-negative (Luminal A/B) tumors express little or no HER2 and are not targets of T-DM1; no trial evidence supports T-DM1 in these HER2-negative subtypes.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.triple-negative/basal-like: Triple-negative/basal-like tumors express little or no HER2 and are not targets of T-DM1; no trial evidence supports T-DM1 in these HER2-negative subtypes.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.intratumoral HER2 heterogeneity: Intratumoral heterogeneity of HER2 (e.g., mixed HER2+/HER2– regions) is described as predicting T-DM1 failure.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.germline BRCA1/2–mutated tumors: Germline BRCA1/2–mutated tumors are often triple-negative; the absence of HER2 in these cases means T-DM1 is inactive, and there is no known interaction between HRD status and T-DM1 sensitivity described.
